name: Feline immunodeficiency virus (FIV)
short_description: An enveloped lentivirus (~100-125 nm) and the cat's own counterpart to HIV — closely related in architecture (envelope, matrix, conical capsid, two RNA copies, reverse transcriptase, integrase) but not infectious to people. Its Env spikes are notably SHORTER and sparser than HIV's, and its Gag proteins carry FIV-specific names (MA p15, CA p24, NC p13) rather than HIV's (p17/p24/p7) — related, not identical.

reference: N/A — no freely-licensed FIV micrograph exists. Searched Wikimedia Commons Category:Feline_immunodeficiency_virus (14 files: genome diagrams, an FIV.svg schematic, a rapid-test-kit photo, a photo of a symptomatic cat — no electron micrograph), CDC PHIL (no FIV entries; its lentivirus EM plates such as #282/#10860/#18142-18143 are consistently HIV-1), and open-access (CC BY) FIV papers on PLOS ONE/Veterinary World (diagnostics/epidemiology only, no EM plates). The one paper located with actual FIV virion/budding TEM figures (J. Virol., PMC2258934) is Copyright American Society for Microbiology, not openly licensed. Per pipeline policy this gap is reported plainly; NO HIV micrograph is substituted and mislabelled as FIV. fetch_reference.py / edit_image.py were not run for this subject — there is nothing to fetch.
